investigations.name: mcom-coculture
investigations.description:
Wraps the `viva_mcom.composites.coculture.mcom_coculture` generator -- a
single `MComReproductionProcess` carrying the whole community. The parameter
set is MCoM's shipped `configs/test.toml`: a Platt P-I phytoplankton
(use_PI_curve, no light-limited exudation) releasing all its labile carbon to
DOC0 and nitrogen to DON0, and a heterotroph that takes up only the labile
DOC0/DON0 (upDOCH=[[1]], upDONH=[[1]]) while its mortality routes a small
fraction (1%) of carbon to a recalcitrant DOC1 pool that nothing consumes.
The community is a clean-room NumPy reproduction of MCoM's Julia engine
(bit-for-bit against upstream golden data -- see `tests/test_golden.py`), so
the succession below is MCoM's own dynamics, not an approximation.

Achieved (200-day run): the phytoplankton blooms from 0.01 to a peak of ~0.84
(1e6 cells/mL) around day 44, then busts as nitrogen runs out; the heterotroph
rises from 0.003 to a peak ~2.39 around day 50 -- lagging the bloom by ~6 days,
the exudate-consumption signature -- and settles near 0.58; inorganic nitrogen
falls from 8.8 mM to below 0.5 mM, with a second-half mean ~1.87 mM. The
labile DOC0 stays low (consumed) while the recalcitrant DOC1 accumulates.
investigations.title: MCoM co-culture: a phytoplankton bloom feeds a heterotroph
investigations.objective:
In a closed (batch) box seeded with a single phytoplankton and a single
heterotroph population, does the MCoM reproduction produce the canonical
phototroph-heterotroph succession -- a phytoplankton bloom that draws down
inorganic nitrogen and, through its exuded dissolved organic carbon and
nitrogen, fuels the growth of a heterotroph that would otherwise have almost
no substrate?

investigations.name: mcom-seasonal
investigations.description:
Wraps the `viva_mcom.composites.coculture.mcom_seasonal` generator -- the same
single-phytoplankton / single-heterotroph parameters as `mcom-coculture`, but
in an open box: dilution rate D = 0.1/day, a constant inflowing DIN
concentration N_ext = 10 mM entering through MCoM's D*(N_ext - N) exchange
term, and a seasonally varying irradiance `5 + sinus(6, 365, 182.5)` (annual
period, summer peak). This exercises MCoM's environmental-fluctuation grammar
(the `sinus` forcing) and its dilution/exchange transport term together.

Achieved (1460-day run, established regime = second half): the phytoplankton
settles into a sustained annual cycle swinging between ~0.42 and ~0.89
(1e6 cells/mL), a peak/trough ratio of ~2.1; the heterotroph tracks it,
oscillating around ~1.86; inorganic nitrogen is held near 2.1 mM (from a 10 mM
inflow), i.e. the community consumes ~80% of the supplied nitrogen. The
community neither washes out nor runs away -- the seasonal light sets the
rhythm, the dilution sets the ceiling.
investigations.title: MCoM under seasonal light: a sustained, oscillating chemostat community
investigations.objective:
When the same MCoM phytoplankton-heterotroph pair is placed in an open,
dilution-driven box (a chemostat) with a steady nutrient inflow but a
sinusoidally varying, annual light supply, does the community reach a
sustained regime that blooms and recedes with the seasons rather than washing
out or running to a fixed point?
